statement: Let phi be the greedy aba-avoiding stack map, and let T be its sorting time. For every integer r>=3, let q be any word using exactly r letters, each occurring twice except that at most one letter may occur three times. Let W be any word whose deletion of a set A of additional letters equals q, with every letter of A occurring in one contiguous nonempty block in W. There is no bound on |A| or on those block multiplicities. Then T(W)=r if and only if T(q)=r. The proof uses a complete 28,800-input computer-assisted base at r=3 and induction on r. In particular, for every run-free q on r>=3 letters, each occurring at least twice, with 2r<=|q|<=2r+1, and every new terminal letter x, T(qx)=r iff T(q)=r. This proves the original first-letter deletion bridge for k>=4; it does not provide the requested complete uniform classification or enumeration M_k of length-2k+2 inputs.
contribution: A maximal-sorting-time invariance principle for arbitrary clumped-letter insertion in the two shortest repeated-letter profiles, with a deletion-closed induction and explicitly exhaustive finite base. It settles the previously unproved terminal-letter reduction needed by the original next-layer problem. Known alphabet-size bounds, truncation compatibility, neighboring counts, and the first-letter-four subclass remain attributed to prior work. No equivalent insertion theorem was located in the bounded primary-source comparison; novelty and substantive value are submitted for fresh review, not certified here.
